title: SpaceX in the S&P 500 would push AI stocks to 51% of the index, strategist says
source_used: Yahoo Finance (original URL, read in full)
key_facts: Strategist Jim Bianco of Bianco Research calculated in an X post that if SpaceX were in the S&P 500, AI-related stocks would be 51% of the index's weight.
If Anthropic and OpenAI also went public before year-end, which the article calls unlikely at least for OpenAI, he put the figure at 55%.
S&P rules require a company to be publicly traded for at least 12 months, so SpaceX is not eligible until June 2027 at the earliest.
Bianco noted the last time a single theme was above 50% of the S&P 500 was the railroads in the 19th century.

Bank of America strategists said this week that peak concentration in most asset bubbles has been capped around 40% of US market value, except the railroad boom; 10 AI stocks now make up 42%, while railroads reached 63%.
The 1873 railroad bust saw 89 of 364 railroads go bankrupt and 18,000 businesses fail in two years, with unemployment at 14% by 1876, per PBS.
quote_evidence: He calculated in a new X post that if SpaceX were currently in the S&P 500, AI-related stocks would be a massive 51% of the index's weight.
"The last time a single theme was >50% of the S&P 500 was the railroads in the 19th century," Bianco noted.
S&P rules require a company to be publicly traded for at least 12 months before it can be added to the storied S&P 500.
why_it_matters_hint: Index funds, and so many savers' pensions, are becoming dominated by one theme.
notes: A hypothetical scenario by one strategist, reported by Yahoo Finance's Brian Sozzi, who also draws the railroad-bust comparison.
